transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2026-03-18
- Start: 14:00 UTC
- Duration: ~62 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Keefe (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Medina (Novus Head of Platform), Anya Petrov (Novus Security Lead), Ravi Kapoor (Novus DevOps), Selina Ho (Novus PM)

Summary (auto): Kickoff to align on SSO/SCIM pattern and RBAC playbook. Agree on one-week pilot to validate SCIM provisioning and role mappings, and to exercise audit logs and KMS with sample data.

[00:00] Maya Chen: ok hi everyone thanks for joining, we'll do a quick agenda run then jump into the playbook, uh feel free to interrupt
[00:18] Carlos Medina: cool yea thanks Maya, we're interested in making sure our SSO is tight and that roles map cleanly, we have SOC2 coming up but also need EU data residency for a subset of projects
[00:33] Liam O'Keefe: great, we'll cover SAML metadata, SCIM mapping, and then propose an RBAC skeleton you can tweak, quick note that we support both SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, and we have contested attributes for groups
[01:02] Anya Petrov: when you say contested attributes — do you mean like group claim naming variations? we've seen different IdPs put group names in different claims and sometimes OIDC versus SAML mismatches
[01:18] Priya Raman: yeah exactly, and SCIM helps normalize that but you still need a canonical ID — we recommend using group UUIDs from the IdP mapped to Redwood role IDs, not free-text names
[01:40] Ravi Kapoor: we plan to have service accounts for automation, what's your guidance on least-privilege for service accounts vs human roles?
[01:56] Liam O'Keefe: separate role families: human roles mapped to SSO groups, service accounts as pinned API keys with narrow scopes, short-lived tokens where possible; discuss KMS-wrapped keys for rotation
[02:18] Selina Ho: quick context — pilot will include three teams: data platform (EU), ingestion (US), and product infra (global). Data residency: EU tenant must store logs and data in EU region, also audit copies for 12 months
[02:40] Maya Chen: noted — we have private deployment options and region pinning for audit logs. For hosted, we support data residency choices; for sensitive EU-only workloads we'd recommend Dedicated or Private with customer-managed KMS
[03:00] Carlos Medina: can you clarify customer-managed KMS? we need BYOK for GDPR controls
[03:14] Liam O'Keefe: BYOK supported — we integrate with your cloud KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, GCP CMEK). Redwood can either use envelope encryption (service keys wrap customer keys) or you can hold root key material in HSM. Important: you must grant decrypt/unwrap to the Redwood operational principal for runtime, or use an on-prem HSM connector in Private mode
[03:46] Anya Petrov: audit trail — what does the event stream look like and how long do you retain it? we want immutable logs forwarded to our Splunk instance
[04:02] Priya Raman: primary audit events include authn/authz decisions, token issuance, SCIM provisioning events, admin changes, and model access logs. Retention configurable; default hosted retention is 90 days, enterprise plans allow 365+ and long term export to your SIEM (S3 -> Splunk/Elasticsearch)
[04:30] Ravi Kapoor: is the log schema documented? we want field names and example events to map to our detection rules
[04:42] Maya Chen: yes we'll share the audit schema doc, it's in the security pack — we'll attach link after call
[05:00] Selina Ho: on SCIM timing — do you support delta syncs vs full? we can't do full syncs every minute
[05:12] Liam O'Keefe: SCIM incremental patch + change tokens. Typical cadence is 5–15 minutes depending on IdP and scale. In the pilot we recommend 10 minutes to validate and then tune
[05:30] Carlos Medina: ok show us an example mapping for roles, like product-infra -> admin-lite?
[05:40] Liam O'Keefe: (shares screen) here's a sample role mapping YAML, note fields: role_id, display_name, allowed_routes, data_scopes. Example: role_id: infra_read, display: infra:read, allowed_routes: ["model-list","logs-read"], data_scopes: ["project:global"]
[06:10] Anya Petrov: I heard you mention logs-read — can we separate metadata access from model prompts content? our compliance team wants prompt content redaction unless explicitly authorized
[06:28] Priya Raman: yes prompts/content are treated as sensitive. We have fields in RBAC to separate metadata/read-only ops from prompt content access. Additional DLP hooks can redact or redact-at-ingest in Private deployments
[06:45] Ravi Kapoor: curious about service account key rotation — do you support automatic rotation? how are old sessions invalidated?
[06:58] Liam O'Keefe: rotate keys at configurable intervals, recommend 24-hour rotation for high-sensitivity keys and 90 days for service keys; sessions tied to token lifetimes and revocation is immediate for API keys if rotated/disabled
[07:20] Carlos Medina: SOC2 and ISO — can you provide our auditors with evidence? encryption diagrams, SOC2 report, penetration test summary?
[07:32] Maya Chen: yes we share SOC2 Type II report, ISO attestation where available, pen test summaries under NDA. We'll walk through the evidence package and redactions as needed
[07:50] Selina Ho: what's the typical on-boarding sequence from Redwood's side?
[07:58] Maya Chen: playbook: 1) exchange SAML metadata and test users, 2) configure SCIM test sync, 3) onboard 10 pilot users across teams, 4) run role smoke tests, 5) validate audit export + KMS wrap, 6) sign off and expand
[08:20] Ravi Kapoor: any gotchas when mapping groups from Azure AD? we use nested groups heavily
[08:30] Priya Raman: nested groups can be flattened during SCIM transform; we recommend establishing canonical group IDs and avoid deep nesting for RBAC-critical roles. If nested, we provide a transform rule engine to expand and dedupe groups
[08:54] Anya Petrov: in multi-region setups, do you replicate role definitions or keep a central control plane?
[09:04] Liam O'Keefe: central control plane with region-scoped enforcement. Role definitions replicate but data enforcement respects region pinning. So the control plane can be global while logs/data stay in region
[09:30] Carlos Medina: ok talk me through prohibited privileges for least-privilege baseline — what do you see commonly over-provisioned?
[09:42] Maya Chen: common over-privilege: broad admin roles that include credential export, full prompt-read access, and model-deploy rights. Baseline we suggest: Admin-lite (config + user management), Ops (deploy/scale but no prompt-read), Audit (read-only logs and billing), Dev (model invoke limited to project scope)
[10:10] Selina Ho: can we do just-in-time elevation for rare admin tasks?
[10:20] Liam O'Keefe: JIT supported via self-service elevation with approval workflows; we can integrate with your ticketing system or SSO-based workflow for temporary role assignment and automatic expiry
[10:40] Ravi Kapoor: how do you handle emergency access for incident response?
[10:48] Priya Raman: emergency break-glass accounts exist but are heavily audited. We suggest MFA on break-glass, session recording, and post-incident review with log snapshots exported to immutable storage
[11:05] Anya Petrov: about export of PII in logs — any masking options?
[11:14] Maya Chen: we have field-level masking and can configure redaction rules; for Private deployments we can run DLP preprocessor to scrub PII prior to persistent storage
[11:30] Carlos Medina: constraints: our timeline is tight — we need pilot results in two weeks for compliance audit prep. Can you commit?
[11:42] Maya Chen: we can run the pilot in 1–2 weeks with a focused scope: SCIM sync + RBAC smoke test + audit export. We'll need your IdP metadata and three test users asap
[11:58] Selina Ho: any limitations on SCIM: group size, users count? we have ~8k employees organization-wide
[12:10] Liam O'Keefe: SCIM scale ok to tens of thousands; best practice is to scope pilot to a single org unit and do bulk provisioning in chunks. For large orgs we enable delta-only syncs and event-driven pushes to avoid spikes
[12:28] Ravi Kapoor: question about RBAC granularity — can we attach data-scoped constraints like project_id list to roles?
[12:38] Priya Raman: yes roles support data_scopes, e.g., allowed_projects: ["eu-data-prod","analytics-sandbox"], and policies can be conditional on IP, region, and time windows
[12:58] Anya Petrov: SIEM integration — do you push raw events or summarized alerts? we prefer raw for forensic purposes
[13:08] Maya Chen: we can push raw events to S3 bucket you manage, or stream to Splunk/Datadog via connector. We also provide summarized alerts for operational dashboards
[13:28] Carlos Medina: about SAML — want to confirm our IdP uses SHA-256 signatures and POST binding, any issues?
[13:38] Liam O'Keefe: supported; we also support HTTP-Redirect and ECDSA keys if needed. We'll validate cert thumbprint during metadata exchange
[13:56] Selina Ho: question — can roles be parameterized so a single role template becomes multiple role instances per project?
[14:06] Priya Raman: templated roles supported; use role templates with variables substituted at provisioning time via SCIM group attributes or external CI/CD pipelines
[14:20] Ravi Kapoor: who usually holds RBAC review responsibility on our side?
[14:28] Carlos Medina: Anya and I will own initial role design, Ravi will handle infra integration
[14:36] Maya Chen: perfect — next we'll run through a quick demo of SCIM sync and role mapping (short)
[14:45] (screen share begins, brief demo noise)
[15:10] Liam O'Keefe: demo notes: I've created a test IdP user, assigned them to 'infra:deployers' group; SCIM patch applied and user appears in Redwood console with role infra:deploy; here's the event in the audit stream: scim.patch -> user.assign -> role.bind
[15:40] Anya Petrov: I see the event but the username looks truncated in transcript, sometimes we see character mangling, is that a transcription artifact?
[15:50] Maya Chen: yes that's transcription, but the console shows full UPN and immutable id
[16:05] Selina Ho: can we export a CSV of role mappings for auditors?
[16:12] Liam O'Keefe: yes exportable; we also provide an evidence bundle with signed timestamps for auditor ingestion
[16:30] Carlos Medina: question about legal/procurement — if we do Dedicated, what's the responsibility split for backups and retention?
[16:42] Maya Chen: in Dedicated, Redwood manages runtime and orchestration; backups for customer data can be customer-managed S3 buckets or provider-managed per contract. We will include responsibilities in the SOW
[16:58] Ravi Kapoor: latency concern — will region pinning increase token latency for EU?
[17:06] Priya Raman: small additional latency due to regional enforcement but typically <15ms; we can run perf tests during pilot to quantify
[17:24] Anya Petrov: can we enable read-only audit snapshots for auditors with time-limited access?
[17:34] Liam O'Keefe: yes time-limited presigned URLs and ephemeral auditor tokens supported, with audit events showing who accessed snapshot
[17:50] Carlos Medina: do you have a recommended least-privilege baseline we can start from?
[17:58] Maya Chen: yes we'll share a baseline matrix: Admin-lite, Ops, Dev, Audit, Service. Each comes with allowed actions and recommended group names to map from IdP
[18:18] Selina Ho: for pilot scoping, we propose: 1) 3 IdP groups mapped to 3 roles, 2) enable audit export to our S3, 3) test KMS BYOK unwrap flow, 4) smoke test role-restricted model calls
[18:36] Liam O'Keefe: sounds good — one technical caveat: BYOK unwrap requires either granting Redwood principal kms:Decrypt on the key or running with Private connector; we'll document both options
[18:58] Anya Petrov: can we get a short runbook for incident scenarios — suspected token exfiltration etc?
[19:08] Priya Raman: yes runbook template included in security pack; includes immediate revocation steps, log snapshot, and investigator contacts
[19:28] Carlos Medina: any blockers we should know of?
[19:36] Maya Chen: main blockers are IdP metadata handoff, firewall rules for SCIM outbound to our endpoint, and KMS permissioning; if those are cleared we can move fast
[19:52] Selina Ho: ok last set of questions — do you support SAML assertion encryption?
[20:00] Liam O'Keefe: yes assertion encryption supported, but requires key exchange and metadata update; we'll include instructions in the SAML guide
[20:18] (brief mute/unmute noises)
[20:30] Maya Chen: recap — action items: we'll send SCIM schema, RBAC baseline matrix, SOC2 report link; you will provide IdP metadata and pilot user list; schedule pilot next week. Anything else?
[20:51] Anya Petrov: can you include example Splunk ingestion config so our SecOps can prep?
[20:58] Priya Raman: yes will include sample HEC config and S3-based raw export instructions
[21:12] Carlos Medina: thanks all, this is actionable, we'll aim to have metadata by Monday
[21:20] Maya Chen: great — Maya out, thanks everyone

(End of transcript — remainder of call covered demo logs and small Q/A)

Notes about transcription: speaker turns occasionally misattributed; a few product names may be transcribed oddly (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache). We will attach original recording to CRM.
questions: How does BYOK work with Dedicated vs Hosted?
What is the default audit retention and how to export to Splunk?
Can SCIM handle nested groups from Azure AD and scale to 8k users?
